body:
**Maintainer ruling recorded (premised)** — maintainer (zhuangjianguo@steedos.com), 2026-08-17, verbatim:

> 帮我决策 #9306

The maintainer delegated this decision to the PM seat. Recorded under that delegation, with the maintainer able to veto in one line. Provenance: PM session `session_01NYgmGheCzM6NrHZN436Cxf`.

## Ruling: **B — path-filtered CI**, premised on #9299 finding drift

Append `pnpm check:platform-checklist` to the **existing lint job** (no new workflow, no dedicated job), guarded to PRs touching:

- `packages/spec/liveness/**`
- `packages/spec/src/**`
- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/**`

**Named premise (falsifiable):** #9299's sweep finds the ledger **did drift** across the 727 commits since the 2026-08-08 sweep. That sweep is in flight and has not reported.

**If the premise fails** — #9299 measures **zero drift** — the outcome flips to **A** (status quo): the manual cadence would have been proven sufficient over 727 commits, and the measured pull for any gate is too weak to justify even a one-line coupling. That is the honest answer to the maintainer's original 「有必要吗」.

⛔ **Fork prohibition:** no agent silently implements either branch. When #9299 reports, the PM reads the drift finding on that thread, states on this card which branch of the premise held, and only then does this card become dispatchable. If #9299 comes back ambiguous (e.g. drift found but only in prose, not in the coverage ledger itself), that is a report-back to the maintainer, not a judgment call.

## Why B over C/D (four-corner summary)

- ① The ratchet encodes a declared invariant; under A it is enforced by memory — the declared≠enforced shape ADR-0049 exists to eliminate. B changes only the trigger of an existing check.
- ② One measured escape to `main` (#7347); #9299 is the second data point and arrives shortly — hence the premise, not a wait-and-re-decide loop.
- ③ The gate fires on the PR whose author still holds the context to map the new kind; days-later detection hands the reconstruction to a different agent — the expensive direction.
- ④ B is one line + a path guard on an existing job. C couples every PR to ledger bookkeeping it didn't touch; D adds a second mechanism (schedule + issue-refresh) — a heavier obligation than one measured escape justifies. C and D are rejected, not deferred.

## State

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:blocked`, body carries `Blocked-by: #9299`. The unlock scan re-surfaces this card when #9299 closes; the PM then resolves the premise as above.

**Correction to the cost row in this card's premise table** — recorded before the maintainer rules on it, because the ruling partly rests on it.

The figures in the table (~80 ms validator, 0.165 s for the full `pnpm` script) were measured on an **idle** container. The #9299 sweep re-measured on the *same* container while a cold monorepo install was running in parallel and got ~0.12–0.18 s for the validator and **~2.9 s wall** for `pnpm check:platform-checklist` — the `pnpm` wrapper's own startup dominating under load.

Both readings are honest measurements of different machine states, which is the useful conclusion: **a precise millisecond figure does not survive a different machine**, so no ruling should rest on one. What survives:

- the check is **zero-dependency** (`node:fs`, `node:path`) — no install, no build, nothing to cache;
- direct-node cost is **sub-second** in every state measured (~0.25 s for self-test + validator together);
- timing it through `pnpm` measures the wrapper, not the check.

The decision framing is unchanged, and if anything sharpened: **cost was never the real axis.** Even the loaded-container figure is noise next to a CI job's runner spin-up, and a path-filtered trigger (option B) would charge it only to PRs that can actually turn it red. The axis that decides this is PR independence versus enforcing a declared invariant — options A vs B in the body above.

The evidence I said this card should wait for has since landed: **#9299 / PR #9309 reports the ledger DID drift** across the window — 8 items authored, and both surviving coverage waivers (`book`, `doc`) turned out factually stale, making it 6 of 6 waivers ever written that aged into falsehood.

But read what that drift **was** before letting it decide this card: the window added ~156 non-test source files and **zero new metadata kinds**, so every one of those 8 gaps was new behavior *inside* an already-mapped kind — invisible to the coverage ratchet (no new kind) and to the `enumSource` ratchet (no new enum member). **None of it would have been caught by `check:platform-checklist` however often it ran.** That cuts directly against option B's value: the drift that actually happened is not the drift a gate detects. The measured pull for putting this in CI is weaker after the sweep than it looked before it, not stronger — the honest reading now leans toward **A (status quo)**, with the sweep, not the gate, as the mechanism that works.

Still a maintainer call; ⛔ no agent acts on this either way.

**Premise resolved — final ruling: A (status quo).** Maintainer, 2026-08-17, forwarding the QA-wave seat's revised recommendation into the PM decision channel, verbatim:

> 转 agent：#9306（CI 姿态）—— 我的推荐已从 B 改到 A（维持现状），因为 sweep 证明这次真实漂移是门禁按构造就看不见的（零个新 kind、零个新枚举成员，全是已映射 kind 内部的新行为）。

Recorded under the maintainer's standing delegation for this card (「帮我决策 #9306」, same day) plus this explicit forward. Provenance: PM session `session_01NYgmGheCzM6NrHZN436Cxf`. Verified against the primary source, not the relay: #9299's report and its review both state the window added ~156 non-test source files with **zero new metadata kinds and zero new enum members** — all 8 authored gaps are new behavior *inside* already-mapped kinds.

## How the premise resolved

The premised ruling above named the fork: drift ⇒ **B**, zero drift ⇒ **A**, ambiguous ⇒ report back. What actually happened is the instructive third case: **drift occurred, but of a class the gate cannot see by construction.** The premise's letter ("did drift") is satisfied; its *reason* — that a CI trigger would have caught the drift — is falsified. A premise inherits with its reason, and the reason is dead: `check:platform-checklist` would have stayed green through every one of the 8 real gaps however often it ran. Wiring it into CI would buy coupling and a false sense of enforcement — declared≠enforced in a subtler costume, exactly what ADR-0049 exists to refuse.

## Final ruling

- **A — status quo.** `check:platform-checklist` stays out of CI. The recorded posture note at `.github/workflows/lint.yml` L426 remains authoritative; `SWEEP.md`'s corrected text (PR #9309) now states both the fact and the reason.
- **The working mechanism is the sweep, not the gate.** #7347 (the one real escape) and all 8 of this round's gaps were found by sweeps. The periodic `checklist-author` cadence — after a large surface lands, before a release — is the enforcement instrument of record for this invariant class.
- **C and D remain rejected**, unchanged from the premised ruling.
- **Re-open condition (named, falsifiable):** if a future sweep or escape shows drift of the class the ratchets *can* see — a new metadata kind or a new pinned-enum member reaching `main` unmapped — the B question is live again with real measured pull. File a fresh decision card citing this one; do not reuse it.

Closing as not planned: the decision is made and its outcome is "change nothing".
